chapter_theme: The wheel of time (கால சக்கரம்): a life is measured out in naazhigai, days, lunar mansions and years, and most people perish without noticing the measure run out. The yogi who rises along the inner staff to the crown outlasts these measures, escapes Yama, and finds the Lord within as the syllable Om and in the seven circles.
structure_note: Counts of time and life (740 to 747); the need for ordered practice and the fate of those who neglect it (748 to 753); the Dancer seen within and the long life it brings (754 to 759); those who never see, and the unpassing thing within the passing (760 to 762); the Lord within, reached as Om and in the seven circles (763 to 769).

740.reading: The nadis form a circle like the moon; taking up the twelve, I set out to examine how life is sustained standing within the Lord's circle and how the nectar slips away.
740.nuance: மதிவட்டம் (the moon's circle), பதிவட்டம் (the Lord's circle) and மது (honey, nectar) are yogic terms I can't fix; ஈராறு (twelve) may be the twelve signs of the time wheel or a count of breath. The plain frame is the poet announcing his inquiry into how life is kept and lost.

741.reading: Whatever people know by the five senses, by understanding, by learning and by mixing these, they perish without noticing the many naazhigai of their life being cut away.
741.nuance: The numbers (ஐந்து, ஆறேழு, எட்டு, ஒன்பது, பத்து) are attached to kinds of knowing and are traditionally taken as counts of the tattvas; I can't fix them. The last line is plain: the naazhigai, units of about twenty-four minutes, run out unnoticed.

742.reading: The years of a perishing life are counted in spans, twenty-five and three, thirty-three, sixty-two, and the hundred that rises beyond reckoning.
742.nuance: ஐயைஞ்சு மூன்று can be read as twenty-five and three or as twenty-eight; what each span measures (a lifetime, a stage, a breath count) is not said.

743.reading: Keeping to the right day and its days, knowing the days one, two, eight and three, and rising by entering into them, one may enter the house without distress.
743.nuance: மனை (house) may be a house of the zodiac, the body, or the inner seat the yogi reaches; the day numbers are not explained.

744.reading: Those who enter the house, bathing in the midst of Magam, reckon twenty-five and twelve; by that they know themselves and climb the eight, with six signs of their own, six of karma and the shining four.
744.nuance: மகம் is the lunar mansion Magha, but bathing there may be literal or a yogic figure. The verse is a list of counts whose scheme I can't recover.

745.reading: Beyond the four, the four beings and the twenty, beyond the ten and the fifteen, beyond forms and qualities and the six years, lies the one beyond the banyan: who knows it?
745.nuance: Each line passes beyond (கடந்தது) a number. ஆலம் may be the banyan, under which Siva teaches, or poison, which he swallowed; பாலம் (bridge) is also unclear. The movement, counting up to what has no count, is plain.

746.reading: Six for the twenty, five for the three, two, twenty-six, and twenty-seven for the one moon: so he ordained the days in another station.
746.nuance: Twenty-seven for the moon matches the twenty-seven lunar mansions. The other numbers, and who விதித்தான் (he who ordained) is, are not given; the Lord is the usual reading.

747.reading: The ordained twenty-eight, with three as a half, gathered make thirty-three; the eighteen set in place, and three, two and one rising in order, are to be known.
747.nuance: A count whose scheme I can't recover. பாரா திகணால் in line 3 is obscure.

748.reading: Unless one examines these orders step by step and practises, it is hard for anyone to remain even a little while; the scripture is the ground, there is no other, so complete it humbly, without beating a drum about it.
748.nuance: மறை may be the Veda or simply the hidden teaching. பறையறையாது (without beating the drum) is a plain instruction against proclaiming one's practice. இருக்க (to remain) is taken here as staying in the body.

749.reading: Fools strive without knowing the end; but for those able to catch the flame as it kindles, like a lamp burning in its bowl, the attainment may be reached even while walking the earth.
749.nuance: இட்ஞ்சில் is taken as இடிஞ்சில் (lamp bowl). கடிந்தனன் மூளக் கதுவ (to seize as it blazes) is obscure; the inner flame of yoga is the usual reading.

750.reading: With the little finger as a cord for the three, held at the chest without moving, and the three at the head joined together, one who contemplates perceives the picture.
750.nuance: This seems to describe a posture or a placing of the fingers, but I can't reconstruct it. ஓவியம் (picture) is taken up in 751 as an inner awareness.

751.reading: Know the awareness that has become this picture; sinners do not know its use; for the three mandalas, the meritorious staff rests in the flower.
751.nuance: தண்டு (staff) is traditionally the spinal channel, பூ (flower) a lotus centre, and the three மண்டலம் those of fire, sun and moon. A plain reading is not available.

752.reading: For the yogi who has run up the staff to the head, the three mandalas gladly accord with the body; those who saw it have seen, and those who did not, the fruit of their deeds, struggle when the body parts.
752.nuance: பிண்டம் பிரிய (when the body separates) is death; the contrast is between the yogi whose body is held in accord and those who die struggling. The variant மகிழ்ந்துடன் changes little.

753.reading: Hear what that struggle and ruin bring: when the sun with the goddess spreads through the six, the life that came with honour falls apart and goes whirling on, ending as food for dogs.
753.nuance: அணங்குடன் ஆதித்தன் ஆறு விரியின் is obscure. சுணங்கன் (dog) is plain: the neglected body ends as carrion.

754.reading: Whirling so, a person never sees the paired flowers and goes into the fire with nothing within; but for those who can see the way to the anklet-feet, the Dancer stands in the channel.
754.nuance: துணைமலர் (paired flowers) and கழல் (anklet) are usually the Lord's feet; தழல் (fire) is the cremation fire. குழல்வழி (the tube's way) is traditionally the central channel.

755.reading: Those who have seen many qualities in the Dancer's sign stand at the head of the sastras; if they look within for experience, the Lord too unfolds as one with them.
755.nuance: ஆத்தன் (the trusted one, the Lord) may be the Dancer or the seer who becomes like him. The contrast between knowing scripture and inner experience (அனுபோகம்) is the verse's turn.

756.reading: Hear now the unending growth in the one: the days go well for the three, and if one stays joined as the thirty pass, the Dancer gleaming like gold on the mountain appears.
756.nuance: The three and the thirty may be mandalas and days of practice; குன்றிடைப் பொன் (gold on the mountain) may be the crown of the head.

757.reading: Knowing the fine point where the Dancer unites, they praise him there; when in ten the eight directions appear and one gazes on the lotus with delight, a hundred years may be attained.
757.nuance: சாத்திடு நூறு (the hundred that is fixed) is taken as a hundred years of life; பதுமரை (lotus) as an inner centre. The numbers ten and eight are not explained.

758.reading: Those who have reached the hundred guard the body and see it held for a thousand; those who stay joined a thousand age on into a crore of yugas.
758.nuance: The plain claim is the long life of the yogi's body, rising in powers of ten. The variant கூடி for கோடி would change a crore of ages to 'joined with the age'.

759.reading: Seeing a crore of ages, they stand unwavering, see crores within without weariness, and staying close in Siva rise to the height.
759.nuance: சிவங்கோடி விட்டு is hard: 'leaving crores for Siva' or 'Siva's crores'. The variant அயர்வற (without weariness) is followed here.

760.reading: Of those who rise, many mingle with the world and take its fruits without knowing, and some act without a mind on it; they do not see the fish-eyed one.
760.nuance: கயலுறு கண்ணி (she with fish-like eyes) is usually the goddess, the Lord's Shakti. Whether உயருறுவார் are failed yogis or simply people who prosper is unclear.

761.reading: Those who do not see run off and pass away; the shameless talk pleasantly and let it go; and for those who do not see, all that has passed passes on unseen.
761.nuance: The verse repeats காணகிலாதார் (those who cannot see) to make blindness to passing time its subject; நயம்பேசி (talking nicely) may mean empty talk in place of practice.

762.reading: Those who cannot see the thing that passes away, yet that passing thing can be seen; and looking within the passing with the mind fixed, the thing that does not pass can be seen.
762.nuance: The verse plays on கழிகின்ற (passing) and கழியாத (unpassing). The passing thing may be the breath, time or the body; the unpassing one is usually the Lord or the self. The turn from one to the other is plain.

763.reading: The unborn one with the eye, seeing within as Nandi, becomes the solitary one in whatever direction one thinks of; this firm Siva-state is the station reached by those able to seek.
763.nuance: கண்ணன் is not Krishna here but is taken as the one with the (third) eye; காணந்தி may be காண் நந்தி (Nandi who sees). சிவகதி (the Siva-state) is plain.

764.reading: For those able to seek there is no Yama and no ruin; they stand as lords among men; this is the thing the seekers have discerned, and it may be told to those able to join it.
764.nuance: நமன் is Yama, death. நரபதி (lord of men) may be literal kingship or mastery; the verse doesn't say.

765.reading: What is spoken is A and U, what is grasped while it stays in the mind; when the spoken M runs along the tube, the Lord settles in the six.
765.nuance: அகார, உகார, மகாரம் are the parts of Om. குழல்வழி (the tube) is the central channel and ஆறு (six) probably the six centres; ஆறு may also mean the way.

766.reading: No one knows where the Lord dwells; for those who search it out he stays within without decay, and whoever sees the Lord becomes him.
766.nuance: அவன் இவன் ஆகுமே can be 'he becomes this one' or 'this one becomes him'; the identity of seer and Lord is the point either way, but how far it goes is the reader's theology.

767.reading: No one knows how he becomes this one; hear it: he unites in this one's sound and light, and stands as this one's circle.
767.nuance: ஓசை (sound) and ஒளி (light) are taken as nada and the inner light; வட்டம் (circle) links to the seven circles of 768.

768.reading: Seven circles blossom within you, yet you do not know how to reach the dwelling of the excellent one; staying attached within and learning the means, you can see his dwelling held firm.
768.nuance: The seven circles (வட்டங்கள் ஏழு) are often taken as the bodily centres; சிட்டன் is the excellent or holy one, the Lord. கட்டி (firmly, or a lump) is unclear.

769.reading: One can see Brahma and Hari, the dark-throated Lord Isa, Sadasiva and Shakti, and all of them set together.
769.nuance: The gods are the usual five presiding deities of the inner centres; the verse may mean they are seen within, in the circles of 768. கலந்துடன் வைத்ததே (what is set mingled together) is vague.

links.note: Both make time the quiet cutter of life: the Kural's day is a saw for those who understand it, Tirumular's naazhigai run out while people know everything else.
Both say that discipline can carry a person past death: the Kural credits the power of austerity, Tirumular the ability to seek the Siva-state within.
Both analyse Om into A, U and M; 1926 adds bindu and nada's end, 765 places M in the inner channel where the Lord settles.
762 says the unpassing thing is found by looking within the passing; 786 says no one knows the perishing thing, and that the poet has come to know the knowing.
724 says Tirumular learned how to nourish the body and so the life; 758 takes the claim to its limit, the yogi's body kept a thousand years and more.

source_issues: 747: line 3 பாரா திகணால் is obscure and may be corrupt.
749: line 2 இட்ஞ்சில் is a misprint, probably for இடிஞ்சில் (lamp bowl).
750: line 3 மூன்றுக்குன்ய் is garbled; variants நின்றிடில் and அணைந்திடும் for நின்றிடும்.
758: the variant கூடி for கோடி changes 'a crore of yugas' to 'joined with the age'.
